blurb: Short-legged Welsh cattle herder with a fox-like head, famed as a royal favorite
description: The Pembroke Welsh Corgi is a small, short-legged cattle herding dog from Wales with erect ears, a fox-like head, a double coat and an alert, eager temperament.
answer: The Pembroke Welsh Corgi is a cattle herding breed from Pembrokeshire, Wales, whose name means dwarf dog in Welsh. It is a small, low-set dog standing about 25 to 30 cm tall and weighing around 9 to 12 kg. It is commonly described as eager to please, alert and family-oriented, though it can be stubborn.

body: The Pembroke is commonly said to trace back to the Flemish settlers of Pembrokeshire after the Norman invasion of Wales, whose continental Spitz-type dogs were used with native Welsh dogs to herd cattle. Pembrokes and Cardigans were first shown together in 1925, recognized by the Kennel Club in 1928, and separated into two breeds in 1934. Queen Elizabeth II owned more than 30 corgis. The breed is popular in the United States but has been listed as vulnerable in the UK.

Compared with the Cardigan, the Pembroke is shorter in body, with smaller ears and slightly straighter legs. It has firm, erect ears and a fox-like head. The double coat ranges from red and sand to brown and black, sometimes with white. Many Pembrokes have docked tails, though docking is illegal in the UK and several registries accept natural tails.

Pembrokes are described as wanting to be involved in family life and eager to learn, though their working background and intelligence can make them stubborn to train. Stanley Coren ranked them 11th for working intelligence. They are alert watchdogs that tend to bark, and young dogs may nip at ankles from herding instinct. Early socialization with people, children and other animals is recommended.

Corgis need both mental stimulation and exercise, as they easily become overweight. They like to run, dig and chase, so a fenced area is advised. The double coat sheds heavily all year, peaking in spring and autumn, but regular brushing keeps it manageable. They compete in agility, obedience, flyball, tracking and herding.

The Pembroke is an achondroplastic, or true dwarf, breed. Conditions reported in the breed include von Willebrand's disease, hip dysplasia, degenerative myelopathy, progressive retinal atrophy, monorchidism and obesity. Genetic testing is available. A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.2 years.

faq.a: Yes. Their double coat sheds heavily all year, with peaks in spring and autumn, though regular brushing keeps it manageable.

faq.q: How long do Pembroke Welsh Corgis live?
faq.a: They typically live about 9 to 15 years; a 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.2 years.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Pembroke and a Cardigan Corgi?
faq.a: The Pembroke is shorter in body, with smaller ears and slightly straighter legs, and the two were recognized as separate breeds in 1934.

faq.q: Are Pembroke Welsh Corgis good with children?
faq.a: Most are described as behaving well around children and other pets, especially with early socialization, though young dogs may herd by nipping at ankles.
